name: Question 14
problem:
Given that for $s>0,$

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t}=\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}},\,L{\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

find the Laplace transform of $f(t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡4t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡4t$ for $s>0.$

$L{f(t)}=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The linearity property of the Laplace transform states that for functions $f(t)$ and $g(t),$ we have

$$
L{\alpha f(t)+\beta g(t)}=\alpha \cdot L{f(t)}+\beta \cdot L{g(t)},
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants.

Taking the Laplace transform and applying the linearity property, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{5\operatorname{cos}⁡4t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡4t} & =L{5\operatorname{cos}⁡4t}+L{-2\operatorname{sin}⁡4t} \\  & =5L{\operatorname{cos}⁡4t}-2L{\operatorname{sin}⁡4t}.\end{aligned}
$$

We are given that

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t} & =\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}}, &  & s>0, \\ L{\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}}, &  & s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{cos}⁡4t} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+16},\,s>0 \\ L{\operatorname{sin}⁡4t} & =\frac{4}{{s}^{2}+16},\,s>0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Laplace transform of $f(t)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =5L{\operatorname{cos}⁡4t}-2L{\operatorname{sin}⁡4t} \\  & =5\cdot \frac{s}{{s}^{2}+16}-2\cdot \frac{4}{{s}^{2}+16} \\  & =\frac{5s}{{s}^{2}+16}-\frac{8}{{s}^{2}+16} \\  & =\frac{5s-8}{{s}^{2}+16}.\end{aligned}
$$

We are given that L{sin⁡ωt}=ωs2+ω2,s>0,L{cos⁡ωt}=ss2+ω2,s>0.

Therefore, we have the following: L{cos⁡4t}=ss2+16,s>0L{sin⁡4t}=4s2+16,s>0

Therefore, the Laplace transform of f(t) is L{f(t)}=5L{cos⁡4t}−2L{sin⁡4t}=5⋅ss2+16−2⋅4s2+16=5ss2+16−8s2+16=5s−8s2+16.
